answer: Fake identities multiply, but the capital cost of each deposit rises like a rising tide, making mass fabrication economically irrational. Sybil resistance comes from staking a bonded deposit at each identity vertex: an agent must lock a scarce, transferable asset before transacting. Reputation accrues only through settled trades, so a fresh node starts worthless. Legitimate actors recover their stake; attackers forfeit it, burning an opal-grade token each cycle and losing their deposit, which makes the attack strictly loss-making. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
